Derivations

This appendix contains derivations from the theory in the body of this book.

Household first order condition for industry-specific consumption demand¶

The derivation for the household first order condition for industry-specific consumption demand (17) is the following:

p~i,t=p~j,s,tαm(ci,j,s,t−cmin,i)αi−1∏u≠iI(cu,j,s,t−cmin,u)αup~i,t(ci,j,s,t−cmin,i)=p~j,s,tαi(ci,j,s,t−cmin,i)αi∏u≠iI(cu,j,s,t−cmin,u)αup~i,t(ci,j,s,t−cmin,i)=p~j,s,tαi∏i=1I(ci,j,s,t−cmin,i)αi=αip~j,s,tcj,s,t \tilde{p}_{i,t} = \tilde{p}_{j,s,t}\alpha_m(c_{i,j,s,t} - c_{min,i})^{\alpha_i-1}\prod_{u\neq i}^I\left(c_{u,j,s,t} - c_{min,u}\right)^{\alpha_u} \\ \tilde{p}_{i,t}(c_{i,j,s,t} - c_{min,i}) = \tilde{p}_{j,s,t}\alpha_i(c_{i,j,s,t} - c_{min,i})^{\alpha_i}\prod_{u\neq i}^I\left(c_{u,j,s,t} - c_{min,u}\right)^{\alpha_u} \\ \tilde{p}_{i,t}(c_{i,j,s,t} - c_{min,i}) = \tilde{p}_{j,s,t}\alpha_i\prod_{i=1}^I\left(c_{i,j,s,t} - c_{min,i}\right)^{\alpha_i} = \alpha_i \tilde{p}_{j,s,t}c_{j,s,t}p~​i,t​=p~​j,s,t​αm​(ci,j,s,t​−cmin,i​)αi​−1u=i∏I​(cu,j,s,t​−cmin,u​)αu​p~​i,t​(ci,j,s,t​−cmin,i​)=p~​j,s,t​αi​(ci,j,s,t​−cmin,i​)αi​u=i∏I​(cu,j,s,t​−cmin,u​)αu​p~​i,t​(ci,j,s,t​−cmin,i​)=p~​j,s,t​αi​i=1∏I​(ci,j,s,t​−cmin,i​)αi​=αi​p~​j,s,t​cj,s,t​

Properties of the CES Production Function¶

The constant elasticity of substitution (CES) production function of capital and labor was introduced by Solow (1956) and further extended to a consumption aggregator by Armington (1969). The CES production function of private capital KKK, public capital KgK_gKg​ and labor LLL we use in Chapter Firms is the following,

Y=F(K,Kg,L)≡Z[(γ)1ε(K)ε−1ε+(γg)1ε(Kg)ε−1ε+(1−γ−γg)1ε(L)ε−1ε]εε−1\begin{aligned} Y &= F(K, K_g, L) \\ &\equiv Z\biggl[(\gamma)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(K)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (\gamma_g)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(K_g)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (1-\gamma-\gamma_g)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(L)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\biggr]^\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1} \end{aligned}Y​=F(K,Kg​,L)≡Z[(γ)ε1​(K)εε−1​+(γg​)ε1​(Kg​)εε−1​+(1−γ−γg​)ε1​(L)εε−1​]ε−1ε​​
(211)

where YYY is aggregate output (GDP), ZZZ is total factor productivity, γ\gammaγ is a share parameter that represents private capital’s share of income in the Cobb-Douglas case (ε=1\varepsilon=1ε=1), γg\gamma_gγg​ is public capital’s share of income, and ε\varepsilonε is the elasticity of substitution between capital and labor. The stationary version of this production function is given in Chapter Stationarization. We drop the mmm and ttt subscripts, the ``  ^  \:\,\hat{}\,\:^‘’ stationary notation, and use the stationarized version of the production function for simplicity.

The Cobb-Douglas production function is a nested case of the general CES production function with unit elasticity ε=1\varepsilon=1ε=1.

Y=Z(K)γ(Kg)γg(L)1−γ−γg Y = Z(K)^\gamma(K_{g})^{\gamma_{g}}(L)^{1-\gamma-\gamma_{g}}Y=Z(K)γ(Kg​)γg​(L)1−γ−γg​
(212)

The marginal productivity of private capital MPKMPKMPK is the derivative of the production function with respect to private capital KKK. Let the variable Ω\OmegaΩ represent the expression inside the square brackets in the production function (211).

MPK≡∂F∂K=(εε−1)Z[Ω]1ε−1γ1ε(ε−1ε)(K)−1ε=Z[Ω]1ε−1(γK)1ε=Z[Ω]1ε−1Z1ε−1[Ω]1ε−1(γK)1εY1ε=(Z)ε−1ε(γYK)1ε\begin{aligned} MPK &\equiv \frac{\partial F}{\partial K} = \left(\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1}\right)Z\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}\gamma^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\right)(K)^{-\frac{1}{\varepsilon}} \\ &= Z\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}\left(\frac{\gamma}{K}\right)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} = \frac{Z\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}}{Z^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}}\left(\frac{\gamma}{K}\right)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}Y^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \\ &= (Z)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\left(\gamma\frac{Y}{K}\right)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \end{aligned}MPK​≡∂K∂F​=(ε−1ε​)Z[Ω]ε−11​γε1​(εε−1​)(K)−ε1​=Z[Ω]ε−11​(Kγ​)ε1​=Zε−11​[Ω]ε−11​Z[Ω]ε−11​​(Kγ​)ε1​Yε1​=(Z)εε−1​(γKY​)ε1​​
(213)

The marginal productivity of public capital MPKgMPK_gMPKg​ is the derivative of the production function with respect to public capital KgK_gKg​.

MPKg≡∂F∂Kg=(εε−1)Z[Ω]1ε−1γg1ε(ε−1ε)(Kg)−1ε=Z[Ω]1ε−1(γgKg)1ε=Z[Ω]1ε−1Z1ε−1[Ω]1ε−1(γgKg)1εY1ε=(Z)ε−1ε(γgYKg)1ε\begin{aligned} MPK_g &\equiv \frac{\partial F}{\partial K_g} = \left(\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1}\right)Z\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}\gamma_g^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\right)(K_g)^{-\frac{1}{\varepsilon}} \\ &= Z\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}\left(\frac{\gamma_g}{K_g}\right)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} = \frac{Z\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}}{Z^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}}\left(\frac{\gamma_g}{K_g}\right)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}Y^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \\ &= (Z)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\left(\gamma_g\frac{Y}{K_g}\right)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \end{aligned}MPKg​​≡∂Kg​∂F​=(ε−1ε​)Z[Ω]ε−11​γgε1​​(εε−1​)(Kg​)−ε1​=Z[Ω]ε−11​(Kg​γg​​)ε1​=Zε−11​[Ω]ε−11​Z[Ω]ε−11​​(Kg​γg​​)ε1​Yε1​=(Z)εε−1​(γg​Kg​Y​)ε1​​
(214)

The marginal productivity of labor MPLMPLMPL is the derivative of the production function with respect to labor LLL.

MPL≡∂F∂L=(εε−1)Z[Ω]1ε−1(1−γ−γg)1ε(ε−1ε)(L)−1ε=Z[Ω]1ε−1(1−γ−γgL)1ε=Z[Ω]1ε−1Z1ε−1[Ω]1ε−1(1−γ−γgL)1εY1ε=(Z)ε−1ε([1−γ−γg]YL)1ε\begin{aligned} MPL &\equiv \frac{\partial F}{\partial L} = \left(\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1}\right)Z\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}(1-\gamma-\gamma_g)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\right)(L)^{-\frac{1}{\varepsilon}} \\ &= Z\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}\left(\frac{1-\gamma-\gamma_g}{L}\right)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} = \frac{Z\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}}{Z^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}\left[\Omega\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon-1}}\left(\frac{1-\gamma-\gamma_g}{L}\right)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}Y^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \\ &= (Z)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\left([1-\gamma-\gamma_g]\frac{Y}{L}\right)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} \end{aligned}MPL​≡∂L∂F​=(ε−1ε​)Z[Ω]ε−11​(1−γ−γg​)ε1​(εε−1​)(L)−ε1​=Z[Ω]ε−11​(L1−γ−γg​​)ε1​=Zε−11​[Ω]ε−11​Z[Ω]ε−11​​(L1−γ−γg​​)ε1​Yε1​=(Z)εε−1​([1−γ−γg​]LY​)ε1​​
(215)

Wages as a function of interest rates¶

The below shows that with the addition of public capital as a third factor of production, wages and interest rates are more than a function of the capital labor ratio. This means that in the solution method for OG-Core we will need to guess both the interest rate rtr_trt​ and wage wtw_twt​.

Y=Z[(γ)1ε(K)ε−1ε+(γg)1ε(Kg)ε−1ε+(1−γ−γg)1ε(L)ε−1ε]εε−1=Z[(γ)1ε(K)ε−1ε(Lε−1εLε−1ε)+(γg)1ε(Kg)ε−1ε(Lε−1εLε−1ε)+(1−γ−γg)1ε(L)ε−1ε]εε−1=ZL[(γ)1ε(KL)ε−1ε+(γg)1ε(KgL)ε−1ε+(1−γ−γg)1ε]εε−1⇒YL=Z[(γ)1ε(KL)ε−1ε+(γg)1ε(KgL)ε−1ε+(1−γ−γg)1ε]εε−1\begin{split} Y &= Z\biggl[(\gamma)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(K)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(K_{g})^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (1-\gamma-\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(L)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\biggr]^\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1} \\ &= Z\biggl[(\gamma)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(K)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{L^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}}{L^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}}\right) + (\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(K_{g})^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{L^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}}{L^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}}\right) + (1-\gamma-\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(L)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\biggr]^\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1} \\ &= ZL\biggl[(\gamma)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{K}{L}\right)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{K_{g}}{L}\right)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}+ (1-\gamma-\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\biggr]^\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1}\\ \Rightarrow\quad \frac{Y}{L} &= Z\biggl[(\gamma)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{K}{L}\right)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{K_{g}}{L}\right)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}+ (1-\gamma-\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\biggr]^\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1} \end{split}Y⇒LY​​=Z[(γ)ε1​(K)εε−1​+(γg​)ε1​(Kg​)εε−1​+(1−γ−γg​)ε1​(L)εε−1​]ε−1ε​=Z[(γ)ε1​(K)εε−1​(Lεε−1​Lεε−1​​)+(γg​)ε1​(Kg​)εε−1​(Lεε−1​Lεε−1​​)+(1−γ−γg​)ε1​(L)εε−1​]ε−1ε​=ZL[(γ)ε1​(LK​)εε−1​+(γg​)ε1​(LKg​​)εε−1​+(1−γ−γg​)ε1​]ε−1ε​=Z[(γ)ε1​(LK​)εε−1​+(γg​)ε1​(LKg​​)εε−1​+(1−γ−γg​)ε1​]ε−1ε​​
(216)
Y=Z[(γ)1ε(K)ε−1ε+(γg)1ε(Kg)ε−1ε+(1−γ−γg)1ε(L)ε−1ε]εε−1=Z[(γ)1ε(K)ε−1ε+(γg)1ε(Kg)ε−1ε(Kε−1εKε−1ε)+(1−γ−γg)1ε(L)ε−1ε(Kε−1εKε−1ε)]εε−1=ZK[(γ)1ε+(γg)1ε(KgK)ε−1ε+(1−γ−γg)1ε(LK)ε−1ε]εε−1⇒YK=Z[(γ)1ε+(γg)1ε(KgK)ε−1ε+(1−γ−γg)1ε(LK)ε−1ε]εε−1\begin{split} Y &= Z\biggl[(\gamma)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(K)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(K_{g})^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (1-\gamma-\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(L)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\biggr]^\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1} \\ &= Z\biggl[(\gamma)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(K)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(K_{g})^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{K^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}}{K^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}}\right) + (1-\gamma-\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}(L)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{K^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}}{K^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}}\right)\biggr]^\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1}\\ &= ZK\biggl[(\gamma)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} + (\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{K_{g}}{K}\right)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (1-\gamma-\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{L}{K}\right)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\biggr]^\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1} \\ \Rightarrow\quad \frac{Y}{K} &= Z\biggl[(\gamma)^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} + (\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{K_{g}}{K}\right)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon} + (1-\gamma-\gamma_{g})^\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\left(\frac{L}{K}\right)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\biggr]^\frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon-1} \end{split}Y⇒KY​​=Z[(γ)ε1​(K)εε−1​+(γg​)ε1​(Kg​)εε−1​+(1−γ−γg​)ε1​(L)εε−1​]ε−1ε​=Z[(γ)ε1​(K)εε−1​+(γg​)ε1​(Kg​)εε−1​(Kεε−1​Kεε−1​​)+(1−γ−γg​)ε1​(L)εε−1​(Kεε−1​Kεε−1​​)]ε−1ε​=ZK[(γ)ε1​+(γg​)ε1​(KKg​​)εε−1​+(1−γ−γg​)ε1​(KL​)εε−1​]ε−1ε​=Z[(γ)ε1​+(γg​)ε1​(KKg​​)εε−1​+(1−γ−γg​)ε1​(KL​)εε−1​]ε−1ε​​
(217)

r=(1−τcorp)(Z)ε−1ε[γYK]1ε−δ+τcorpδτ r = (1 - \tau^{corp})(Z)^\frac{\varepsilon-1}{\varepsilon}\left[\gamma\frac{Y}{K}\right]^\frac{1}{\varepsilon} - \delta + \tau^{corp}\delta^\taur=(1−τcorp)(Z)εε−1​[γKY​]ε1​−δ+τcorpδτ

As can be seen from (218) and (219), the wage www and interest rate rrr are functions of Y/LY/LY/L and Y/KY/KY/K, respectively. Equations (216) and (217) show that both Y/LY/LY/L and Y/KY/KY/K are functions of the capital-labor ratio K/LK/LK/L, the public-capital-labor ratio, Kg/LK_{g}/LKg​/L, and the public-private capital ratio, K/KgK/K_{g}K/Kg​. We cannot solve these equations for rrr and www solely as functions of the same ratios.

In the Cobb-Douglas unit elasticity case (ε=1\varepsilon=1ε=1) of the CES production function, the first order conditions are:

if   ε=1:w=(1−γ−γg)Z(KL)γ(KgL)γg \text{if}\:\:\,\varepsilon=1:\quad w = (1-\gamma-\gamma_g)Z\left(\frac{K}{L}\right)^\gamma \left(\frac{K_{g}}{L}\right)^{\gamma_{g}}ifε=1:w=(1−γ−γg​)Z(LK​)γ(LKg​​)γg​
(220)
if   ε=1:r=(1−τcorp)γZ(KgK)γg(LK)1−γ−γg−δ+τcorpδτ \text{if}\:\:\:\varepsilon=1:\quad r = (1 - \tau^{corp})\gamma Z\left(\frac{K_{g}}{K}\right)^{\gamma_{g}}\left(\frac{L}{K}\right)^{1-\gamma-\gamma_{g}} - \delta + \tau^{corp}\delta^\tauifε=1:r=(1−τcorp)γZ(KKg​​)γg​(KL​)1−γ−γg​−δ+τcorpδτ
(221)

Again, even if this simple case, we cannot solve for rrr as a function of www for the reasons above.

Sparsity of the household equation Jacobian¶

Holding fixed the prices and policies a type-jjj cohort faces, its 2S2S2S stationarized necessary conditions (143), (144), and (145) in the 2S2S2S unknowns {nj,s,b^j,s+1}s=E+1E+S\{n_{j,s},\hat b_{j,s+1}\}_{s=E+1}^{E+S}{nj,s​,b^j,s+1​}s=E+1E+S​ have a banded Jacobian. From the budget constraint (142), stationarized consumption at age sss depends on only three unknowns,

c^j,s=1p[(1+rp)b^j,s+w^ ej,s nj,s−tax^j,s−egyb^j,s+1]+Xj,s, \hat c_{j,s} = \frac{1}{p}\Bigl[(1+r_p)\hat b_{j,s} + \hat w\,e_{j,s}\,n_{j,s} - \widehat{tax}_{j,s} - e^{g_y}\hat b_{j,s+1}\Bigr] + X_{j,s},c^j,s​=p1​[(1+rp​)b^j,s​+w^ej,s​nj,s​−taxj,s​−egy​b^j,s+1​]+Xj,s​,
(222)

where tax^j,s\widehat{tax}_{j,s}taxj,s​ depends only on (b^j,s,nj,s)(\hat b_{j,s}, n_{j,s})(b^j,s​,nj,s​) through labor and capital income (already in the active set, so it adds no further coupling), and Xj,sX_{j,s}Xj,s​ collects terms fixed in the inner solve (bequests bq^j,s\hat{bq}_{j,s}bq^​j,s​, remittances rm^j,s\hat{rm}_{j,s}rm^j,s​, government transfers tr^j,s\hat{tr}_{j,s}tr^j,s​, UBI ubi^j,s\hat{ubi}_{j,s}ubi^j,s​, the pension benefit θj\theta_jθj​, and the c^min,i\hat c_{min,i}c^min,i​ terms). The labor Euler equation (143) at age sss therefore depends on {b^j,s,b^j,s+1,nj,s}\{\hat b_{j,s},\hat b_{j,s+1},n_{j,s}\}{b^j,s​,b^j,s+1​,nj,s​} alone, and the savings Euler equation (144)---which links c^j,s\hat c_{j,s}c^j,s​ to b^j,s+1\hat b_{j,s+1}b^j,s+1​ and c^j,s+1\hat c_{j,s+1}c^j,s+1​---depends on {b^j,s,b^j,s+1,b^j,s+2,nj,s,nj,s+1}\{\hat b_{j,s},\hat b_{j,s+1},\hat b_{j,s+2},n_{j,s},n_{j,s+1}\}{b^j,s​,b^j,s+1​,b^j,s+2​,nj,s​,nj,s+1​}. The marginal tax rates τsmtrx\tau^{mtrx}_sτsmtrx​ and τs+1mtry\tau^{mtry}_{s+1}τs+1mtry​ are functions of own-age income (already in these sets), so they add no further coupling, and the terminal condition (145) is sparser still. Each of the 2S2S2S equations therefore depends on at most five of the 2S2S2S unknowns, regardless of SSS, so the Jacobian has at most 10S10S10S nonzero entries rather than the (2S)2=4S2(2S)^2 = 4S^2(2S)2=4S2 of a fully coupled system. This is the per-cohort counterpart to the dense 2JS2JS2JS system noted at the start of Chapter Equilibrium: cohorts couple only through prices, which are held fixed in the inner solve. A finite-difference Jacobian can then be built from a number of evaluations set by the bandwidth---about seven at S=80S = 80S=80---rather than 2S2S2S, by probing together unknowns that affect no common equation (Figure Figure 4).
